item.itunes:title: 蔣萬安最害怕的里長來了！會勘還在搞政治鬥爭，北市府為何蔣不聽？｜大安文山市議員候選人 ⑨ 陳峙穎 × 時事評論員周偉航午餐大時客 EP.94 精華片段

item.itunes:summary:
https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=y5c83hZaZZg

值得閱讀的理由

  • 呈現作者對文山區颱風期間勘查行程的質疑，以及地方官員通知流程的重要性。
  • 透過「臨時通知」的情境比喻，說明作者為何認為自己遭到指責並不公平。
  • 記錄作者對市長現場應對、後續承諾與災後清掃安排的批評，展現其對市政執行的追問。

摘要

文山勘查行程與通知爭議

作者談到文山區的現場勘查，認為行程原本是由議員鍾沛君主導，市長蔣萬安則像是被帶去陪同的「人形看板」。作者批評市長在現場顯得茫然，並質疑勘查前沒有通知里長，讓熟悉地方情況的人無法事先說明問題與現況。作者表示，過去類似行程通常會提前通知，因此這次的安排令他感到自己像是被刻意設局。

作者反駁「已通知卻未到場」

面對鍾沛君事後稱作者已接獲通知、卻沒有出席的說法，作者以節目錄影作比喻：若原定中午開錄，直到十一點四十五分才通知來賓，來賓趕到後又被指責遲到，顯然並不公平。作者據此強調，現場勘查理應事先通知，並指控這次行程沒有通知，較像是一場政治宣傳行程。他也批評鍾沛君散播不實說法、試圖影響輿論。

市長現場回應與後續承諾

作者回憶，自己在現場提出問題後，市長只表示會處理，卻沒有說明相關單位為何遲遲未解決，也沒有交代明確時程。作者追問是否會有主管官員到場，以及何時能處理，市長一度轉向副市長張文德尋求協助；副市長也僅表示會處理。作者說，一週過去仍在等待後續聯繫，因此質疑市府承諾是否有實際進度。

批評災後清掃與市政作風

作者進一步質疑市長在颱風期間安排勘查，以及颱風過後與清潔人員一同掃街的用意，認為相關行動可能更重視拍照與營造效果，而非提出具體治理成果。他也批評市長掃地的畫面反而暴露其不熟悉工作方式，並將這些安排形容為臨時起意、缺乏規劃。

呼籲檢視市政表現

作者表示，執政者說要專注市政並不足夠，市民仍應檢視實際治理成效；他認為市長面對問題時缺乏清楚回應，並呼籲大安、文山選民集中支持候選人陳志瑜。節目最後，作者感謝觀眾收看，並邀請大家持續關注、按讚、訂閱及支持他認為值得支持的政黨與候選人。

================================================

As for Chung Pei-chun, I won't even go there; I think she's just bad, truly wicked, deliberately trying to stir up public opinion. >> Let me be direct: this site inspection in Wenshan was meant for Chung Pei-chun ; Chiang Wan-an was basically just brought in as a human cardboard cutout. I really felt that day that the mayor— well, let's just say the mayor is really hollow, he’s like a baby, he just doesn’t have a clue. >> You could tell by his lost, dazed look as he stared at me like this. >> You know, just with his mouth open, and then— >> He just didn't know; first, he didn't know who you were, and second, he didn't.

know why things were the way they were here. >> Because he was only here to serve as a human cardboard cutout. >> First point, the first issue, which has been quite popular lately: inspecting during a typhoon without notifying the ward chief. In my humble opinion, back when I was a director, how could there be a site inspection without the ward chief? Usually, a councilor would tell the ward chief, "We're coming here for an inspection." They are familiar with local affairs and can tell you anytime what’s going on here and what’s not a problem there. If he wants to come, he can come, but if.

you're coming to film a place that is relatively unflooded and clean, that's fine, but you should provide a channel for me to respond, shouldn't you? Every time they came in the past, they would notify me first thing in the morning or even the day before, saying, "Hey, someone is coming to inspect tomorrow," or "someone is coming today. " It had always been like that, so this time I really feel like I was being set up. >> Because afterward, he kept— >> Wait, let me ask: can you say whether councilors from other parties went? >> Hey, other parties—I mean, did anyone.

from the mayor's own party, the DPP, attend? >> No. >> No, there was no notification; it was just a campaign trip. >> They keep dodging this question, but there really was no notification; it was a campaign trip. That's right, it was purely a campaign trip. So, once I got to the scene, since they had no intention of answering the question, I called them out directly, specifically Councilor Chung Pei-chun, who later posted things to attack me. Let me ask you about this situation: since I've been constantly smeared by Chung Pei-chun afterward, and she keeps insisting that I was notified and that I just didn't show up. Let me set up a scenario.

We’re here in this studio for the " Lunchtime Moment." If I were the host and didn't notify you beforehand—we start at 12: 00—and I called you at 11:45 saying, "Hey, Professor Xiao, we have our 'Lunchtime Moment' livestream recording today." >> Where would you be? And then, after you rushed over and ended up five minutes late, I said, " Hey, Professor Xiao, what’s wrong with you? We notified you. How could you be late? I got to the site and you weren't there.

." Hmm. >> How would you feel? >> Zhong Peijun is just talking nonsense. Site visits always have notifications. The Mayor mobilizes so many people, yet you didn't give prior notice? Not to mention Zhong Peijun—I think she’s just malicious, truly malicious, deliberately trying to sway public opinion. >> To put it bluntly, this site visit in Wenshan was meant for Zhong Peijun. Honestly, he’s just a cardboard cutout she brought along. >> That day, I felt the Mayor...well, the Mayor is really hollow. What is even going on? >> He’s just like a baby; he has no clue about anything.

>> His eyes were just so blank, like he was looking at me, you know. >> You know, just like that, with his mouth open. He didn't know—first, he didn't know who you were, and second, he didn't know why things were like this. >> Because he was only there to serve as a cardboard cutout. He looked at his entourage, and they stepped in to shield him. Afterward, since I still insisted on voicing my concerns, I tried my best to hold my ground and say what I needed to say. >> After I finished speaking, he still looked completely lost and said, "We will handle it." Then I asked, "Mayor, for this part you’re handling, will a relevant official be coming down?" We’ve had many site visits; if the department.

could handle it, they would have done so already. But you couldn’t even explain why it hasn't been dealt with. He looked panicked and turned to Deputy Mayor Zhang Wend-de next to him, looking for help. Zhang Wend-de then jumped in and said, "Ah, we’ll handle it." I didn't ask you; I want to know by what date. >> Exactly, exactly. >> Reporting to you, it’s already been a week. I’ve been waiting all week to see when our Deputy Mayor would contact me, but as of now, I’m still waiting for that person. Personally, I find it baffling that he would schedule such an itinerary on a typhoon day; what kind of effect is he trying to create? Same.

thing after the typhoon, him sweeping the streets; what effect is he going for ? He even made all the sanitation workers stay to sweep with him just for a photo op, all while moving numbers around. I mean, why would you even do something like that? >> The only effect was that the whole of Taiwan saw he doesn't know how to use a broom; everyone saw he couldn't even sweep properly. >> Everything is so last-minute; can we stop with the last-minute stuff? How is everything so improvised? Suddenly starting a cleanup, suddenly opening a campaign headquarters. >> He’ll say he’s focused on city governance. We agree with focusing on city governance since he’s the incumbent.

, but the point is we need to examine that governance; if you say you’re focused, have you actually done a good job? That’s what we’re questioning. How could he possibly be focused on all the city's problems? You ask him three questions and he knows nothing. Everyone , please unite! Da'an and Wenshan districts, please consolidate your votes and support our candidate, number nine, Chen Chih-yu, okay? Alright, we'll end here today. Thank you everyone, bye-bye . >> Thank you. >> Thank you all for watching today. I hope you'll continue to support good candidates. Don't forget to follow, like , subscribe, and hit the notification bell to keep watching Lunchtime Hour.

Please also show your support for more good political parties and candidates. Thanks everyone!

摘要

文山勘查行程與通知爭議

作者談到文山區的現場勘查，認為行程原本是由議員鍾沛君主導，市長蔣萬安則像是被帶去陪同的「人形看板」。作者批評市長在現場顯得茫然，並質疑勘查前沒有通知里長，讓熟悉地方情況的人無法事先說明問題與現況。作者表示，過去類似行程通常會提前通知，因此這次的安排令他感到自己像是被刻意設局。

作者反駁「已通知卻未到場」

面對鍾沛君事後稱作者已接獲通知、卻沒有出席的說法，作者以節目錄影作比喻：若原定中午開錄，直到十一點四十五分才通知來賓，來賓趕到後又被指責遲到，顯然並不公平。作者據此強調，現場勘查理應事先通知，並指控這次行程沒有通知，較像是一場政治宣傳行程。他也批評鍾沛君散播不實說法、試圖影響輿論。

市長現場回應與後續承諾

作者回憶，自己在現場提出問題後，市長只表示會處理，卻沒有說明相關單位為何遲遲未解決，也沒有交代明確時程。作者追問是否會有主管官員到場，以及何時能處理，市長一度轉向副市長張文德尋求協助；副市長也僅表示會處理。作者說，一週過去仍在等待後續聯繫，因此質疑市府承諾是否有實際進度。

批評災後清掃與市政作風

作者進一步質疑市長在颱風期間安排勘查，以及颱風過後與清潔人員一同掃街的用意，認為相關行動可能更重視拍照與營造效果，而非提出具體治理成果。他也批評市長掃地的畫面反而暴露其不熟悉工作方式，並將這些安排形容為臨時起意、缺乏規劃。

呼籲檢視市政表現

作者表示，執政者說要專注市政並不足夠，市民仍應檢視實際治理成效；他認為市長面對問題時缺乏清楚回應，並呼籲大安、文山選民集中支持候選人陳志瑜。節目最後，作者感謝觀眾收看，並邀請大家持續關注、按讚、訂閱及支持他認為值得支持的政黨與候選人。
